conviction_note: Event confirmed by the issuer's own 2026 calendar (Tuesday 10 Nov board, Q3 'informazioni periodiche aggiuntive'), released in session as Q1 (13:36) and H1 (14:05) were. Q3 numbers are new and no numeric guidance exists, so abs_move sits near the 7% 'new numbers' base, nudged up for $150k/day turnover and three straight prints that moved 9-12%. Nothing unpriced and company-level decides the sign. Sofar's first full quarter mechanically lifts reported revenue about 11% y/y, but analysts model it. Against that: leverage of 2.7x against a 3.0x covenant, gearing of 46% against a 40% policy, a buyback cut to a token since 14 Sep, and a reaction function that has sold the last three prints even when they were 'in line'. So p_up is 45 and the scaled number is -0.75. The findings sum to -0.2 because each is a small proxy or a known mechanical item; the gap from the scaled number is the reaction history, which moves only p_up.

already_public.what: Board date: Tuesday 10 November 2026, approval of 'Informazioni periodiche aggiuntive al 30 settembre 2026' (issuer's 2026 corporate calendar, image PDF read by rendering)

H1 2026: revenue EUR124.8m (-3.1%), adj EBITDA EUR15.2m (12.2% vs 16.8%), Q2 Nutra -3.5% after Q1 -17.9%, Cosmetics Q2 -17.9% (client insourcing), NFP EUR98m, Sofar consolidated from 1 Jun 2026; pro-forma H1 with Sofar from 1 Jan: revenue EUR138.6m, adj EBITDA EUR17.9m; H2 outlook 'approccio prudente', no numeric guidance

Q3 2025 comparison base, derived from 9M25 (rev EUR189.7m, adj EBITDA EUR30.5m) minus H1 2025 (EUR128.7m, EUR21.6m): Q3 2025 revenue about EUR61.0m, adj EBITDA about EUR8.9m (14.6%); all three BUs grew in Q3 2025, Nutra +4.9%

Intermonte after H1: TP 13 -> 11, Outperform; revenue estimates cut 4-5%; FY26 adj EBITDA margin 13.5% (from 14.9%) with sequential H2 improvement; the ~EUR40m EBITDA previously expected for 2026 pushed to 2027
Intesa Sanpaolo after H1: TP 12.8 -> 10.8, Buy; H1 adj EBITDA 'sostanzialmente in linea con le nostre stime'

new_in_release.expect: Q3 revenue up about 10-13% y/y on the first full quarter of Sofar (about EUR8m a quarter at the H1 pro-forma run-rate), with organic growth flat to slightly negative. Adj EBITDA about flat y/y near EUR9m against a broker path that implies sequential margin improvement toward ~14.5% in H2. Slight miss risk on margin, and the revenue headline turns positive.
Net debt at 30 Sep against EUR98m at June, and NFP/EBITDA against the 3.0x covenant (2.7x at June). Working capital and capex are the risk; it leans negative.
No numeric guidance is given. Qualitative H2 wording after 'prudente': unknown, most likely repeated.
Q4 commentary on Nutra weight-control destocking and the Brembate ramp: unknown
Any statement on the buyback, which has been at a token pace since 14 Sep with no purchases after 16 Oct: unknown

The nearest sourced bar is Intermonte's FY26 adj EBITDA margin of 13.5% with sequential H2 improvement (https://www.teleborsa.it/News/2026/09/09/fine-foods-intermonte-taglia-target-price-ostacoli-temporanei-rallentano-la-ripresa-89.html), which against H1's 12.2% implies about 14.5% in H2. Every finding is capped small for this reason.
session_check: bmo (window-equivalent). The release lands IN SESSION on the event day, not before the open, so close(2026-11-09) -> close(2026-11-10) holds the whole reaction. The issuer's own press-release timestamps show the Q1 2026 release at 13:36 on 07/05/2026 and H1 at 14:05 on 08/09/2026; Teleborsa ran H1 at 14:34 on 8 Sep. Both days' closes carried the moves (-9.15%, -9.44%). Sources: https://www.finefoods.it/investor-relations-comunicati-stampa/ and https://www.teleborsa.it/DettaglioNews/127_2026-09-08_TLB/Fine-Foods-il-nuovo-sito-produttivo-di-Brembate-pesa-sui-conti-del-primo-semestre.html
positioning_check: The CONSOB posizioni nette corte register was read on 2026-11-06 and does not name Fine Foods: 0.0%, the 0.5% truncation floor, not a measurement. anchor_covered is false, so there is no positioning anchor and priced_lean_pct (+0.44) is the run-up term alone. Building or covering is not knowable. The one disclosed flow is the issuer's own buyback. It ran at 17,500-25,000 shares a week (about EUR130-150k) through 11 Sep, fell to 250 shares a week from 14 Sep, and the October Allegato 3F shows no purchases after 16 Oct (treasury 12.09%).

findings.finding: Q3 2026 is the first full quarter with Sofar consolidated (consolidated from 1 Jun 2026). At the H1 pro-forma run-rate (EUR13.8m revenue and EUR2.7m adj EBITDA for Jan-May) that adds about EUR8m of revenue and EUR1.6m of adj EBITDA against Q3 2025's EUR61.0m / EUR8.9m. Reported revenue should therefore print up about 10-13% y/y, the first positive y/y headline after Q1 -7.2% and H1 -3.1%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue-led headlines have not saved this name. H1 (-3.1% revenue, 'in line' per Intesa) fell 9.44% on 2026-09-08, Q1 (-7.2%) fell 9.15% on 2026-05-07, and FY25 fell 11.81% on 2026-03-12. Q3 2025, with all BUs growing, fell 2.57% on 2025-11-06.
findings.original_quote: I ricavi consolidati e l'EBITDA Adj. pro-forma, con l'assunzione convenzionale del consolidamento di Sofar S.p.A. dal 1 gennaio 2026, ammontano rispettivamente a €138,6 milioni e a €17,9 milioni. [...] 1Sofar S.p.A. consolidata dal 1 giugno 2026 (Consolidated revenue and pro-forma adj EBITDA, assuming Sofar consolidated from 1 Jan 2026, are EUR138.6m and EUR17.9m; Sofar consolidated from 1 Jun 2026)
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Both covering brokers model Sofar, which is why this is small. What is not priced is the wire headline. Teleborsa's last three headlines on this name read 'in calo' or 'pesa sui conti', and on a $150k/day name with retail-heavy flow a 'ricavi in crescita a doppia cifra' headline is a different first read. If that were priced, the stock would not have drifted -8.8% over 20 sessions into a print with a mechanically positive top line.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 base computed from the issuer's own 9M25 release: https://cdn.financialreports.eu/financialreports/media/filings/4495/2025/RNS/4495_rns_2025-11-06_761186e0-5ab6-447d-b7c8-5a44156d9a9a.pdf

findings.finding: Capital is tight going into the print. At 30 Jun NFP/adj EBITDA was 2.7x against a 3.0x covenant on several term loans, tested semi-annually, and gearing was about 46% against a stated policy ceiling of 40%. The buyback (EUR12m spent in H1) was cut to 50 shares a day from 14 Sep and stopped after 16 Oct. A Q3 NFP that rises, or EBITDA that does not recover, would bring the December covenant test into view.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not isolable. NFP went from EUR47.9m to EUR98m at H1 and that print fell 9.44%, but the release also carried the margin and impairment news.
findings.original_quote: La politica del Gruppo consiste nel mantenere questo rapporto inferiore al 40%. A causa dell'operazione straordinaria, nel primo semestre 2026 tale rapporto si attesta attorno al 46% [...] Alla data del 30 giugno 2026, il covenant, la cui soglia è pari a 3, risulta essere rispettato. [...] Posizione Finanziaria Netta/Ebitda adj. 2,7 (Group policy keeps gearing below 40%; because of the extraordinary transaction it is about 46% at H1 2026. At 30 June 2026 the covenant, threshold 3, is met. NFP/adj EBITDA 2.7)
findings.why_not_priced: The covenant threshold and the 46% gearing sit on page 65 and in the notes of the half-year report, not in the press release or either broker headline. The buyback throttle only shows up by reading weekly notices side by side. Financing is a question here, and the answer is benign in purpose: the debt bought Sofar and the Brembate ramp, and Pharma grew +5.7% organic. The risk is headroom, not distress, so the size is small and the range is skewed. If the market had fully priced a covenant concern, it would show in a discount to peers wider than the current ~7x EV/LTM EBITDA (an estimate, not sourced).
findings.independence: The buyback notices show the throttle independently: week to 11 Sep 17,500 shares, EUR132,722 (https://www.finefoods.it/investor-relations-comunicati-stampa/); week 12-16 Oct 250 shares, EUR1,635 (https://www.finefoods.it/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/265-CS-ACQUISTO-AZIONI-PROPRIE-16.10.2026-ITA.pdf); October Allegato 3F with the last purchase on 16/10 (https://www.finefoods.it/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/2026_11_02_Allegato-3F-Fine-Foods-ottobre-2026.pdf)

findings.finding: Herbalife, which Fine Foods names as a client, reported Q3 2026 EMEA net sales of $259.0m, -4.9% reported and -5.2% in local currency, after about -6% ex-FX in Q2. European demand from a weight-management customer is still contracting at an unchanged rate, consistent with the Nutra weakness Fine Foods already disclosed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nutra drove the last three negative prints: Q1 Nutra -17.9% and the stock -9.15%; H1 Nutra -10.9% and the stock -9.44%.
findings.why_not_priced: A counterparty that spoke after Fine Foods last did. Nobody covering FF publishes a Herbalife read-through. The transmission is a hypothesis: Fine Foods does not disclose Herbalife's share, only that its top five clients are 56.7% of revenue. The trend is unchanged rather than worse, so the finding is small. A third-party summary, not Herbalife's own table, so snippet-grade.
findings.independence: Fine Foods lists Herbalife among its clients in the H1 2026 report (https://www.finefoods.it/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Relazione-finanziaria-30.06.2026-v.-08.09-Clean-con-opinion.pdf). Herbalife Q2 2026 EMEA -6.0% ex-FX per its press release (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260805819129/en/).

findings.finding: Intercos, the Italian cosmetics CDMO peer, reported a record Q3 2026: revenue EUR294.2m, +12.9% (12% at constant FX), adj EBITDA +7.5%, with double-digit growth expected in Q4. Outsourced cosmetics demand in Italy is strong, so Fine Cosmetics' weakness (Q2 -17.9%) is client-specific insourcing rather than the market.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cosmetics is 11.6% of revenue and has never been the identifiable driver of an FF move.
findings.original_quote: Intercos ha registrato nel terzo trimestre ricavi record a 294,2 milioni di euro (Intercos posted record third-quarter revenue of EUR294.2m)
findings.why_not_priced: A peer proxy for a segment whose stated problem is idiosyncratic (a large client insourcing). Net of the rest of the company it is almost nothing, which is why it is +0.1. Recorded because it is the one Italian counterparty series that reported after Fine Foods did.
findings.independence: Fine Foods' own explanation of the Cosmetics decline as client insourcing in the H1 release: https://www.finefoods.it/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/FF_Comunicato-Stampa-H1-2026.pdf

findings.finding: Management has already lowered the bar for H2 in writing: 'mantenere un approccio prudente sulle attese per la seconda parte dell'esercizio'. A flat-to-soft Q3 lands inside what the company told the market to expect.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 'prudente' wording arrived with H1, which fell 9.44% on the day and a further 8% over the next three sessions.
findings.original_quote: Pur confermando la validità del modello diversificato su tre segmenti, Fine Foods ritiene opportuno mantenere un approccio prudente sulle attese per la seconda parte dell'esercizio, alla luce della limitata visibilità in alcuni mercati di riferimento. (While confirming the three-segment model, Fine Foods considers it appropriate to keep a prudent approach to expectations for the second half, given limited visibility in some markets.)
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock has fallen from 8.26 to 6.06 since. It is filed because it sets the bar the Q3 release will be read against. Intermonte's 'sequential H2 improvement' assumption sits above the company's own wording, so whatever is unpriced here is in the gap between the two, and it is small.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Websim headline 'Fine Foods investe 60 milioni in uno stabilimento Alfasigma' read as a new EUR60m investment
rejected_candidates.detail: The article's own text ties the ~EUR60m to the new plant, while the issuer's H1 release puts the Sofar purchase at EUR27.0m and Brembate at the ~EUR50m sourced elsewhere. It is a conflated headline, not a new capex commitment.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Three consecutive prints sold 9-12% (12 Mar -11.81%, 7 May -9.15%, 8 Sep -9.44%)
rejected_candidates.detail: Reaction history, not a fact about this print. Carried in p_up and abs_move_pct and in each finding's reaction_history field rather than counted as a finding.

baseline_tension: The findings net slightly negative and agree with the -8.8% 20-day and -29.8% 60-day run-up rather than cutting against it. The lean (+0.44, run-up only, no short anchor) points mildly up on mean-reversion, and nothing found gives a reason to bet on that reversion.
language_note: Everything load-bearing was Italian-only: the issuer's 2026 calendar (image PDF) confirming 10 Nov, and the press-release timestamps that settle the in-session release time.
The covenant threshold (3.0x), leverage 2.7x and 46% gearing against the 40% policy sit only in the Italian half-year report; no English source carries them.
The buyback throttle from ~EUR140k a week to 250 shares a week and then zero shows only in the Italian weekly 'informativa' notices and the Allegato 3F.
Broker views (Intermonte FY26 margin 13.5%, H2 sequential improvement; Intesa 'in linea') came only through Teleborsa in Italian.
The English sources added only the Herbalife Q3 EMEA counterparty number.
lessons_applied: 'Right about the number and too small about the move': Q3 numbers are not pre-released and the name's last three prints moved 9-12%, so abs_move_pct went from 6.5 to 7.5. The reaction history stays in p_up (45), not in the size.

'Financing is a question': the debt bought Sofar and the Brembate ramp, and Pharma grew +5.7% organic, so the leverage finding went from -0.6 to -0.5 with a skewed range rather than a distress-sized number.
'A finding the market has been told is worth ~0': the Sofar consolidation is mechanically known and modelled, so it went from +0.4 to +0.3.
'Cash can outweigh': this confirmed the working-capital/NFP line as the main risk in new_in_release; no number changed beyond the above.
